newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian bourse to launch index Oct 17.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian bourse to launch index Oct 17.

text.p: The stock exchange of the Baltic state of Lithuania is to launch its own stock index from October 17, based on a model drawn up by the World Bank's International Finance Corp, a stock exchange spokeswoman said on Wednesday.
"It will cover a substantial part of the market but we cannot say in advance which companies will be listed as it might affect their price," the spokeswoman told Reuters.

Lithuania was ahead of neighbours Latvia and Estonia in launching a stock market in 1993 but a lack of transparency, the lack of large and liquid companies plus a recent banking crisis have kept trading volumes down.
The market, which trades twice a week, has so far been tracked only by Lithuanian securities' houses own indices.
The stock exchange spokeswoman said that if demand picked up, trading may take place three times a week.
"The official index should attract additonal interest and hopefully investment in the market," one trader said.
"It will make the market more transparent and give investors a clearer view of what is happening," he added.
